habitat: Pairs and small parties breed in reed beds and the bush beside rivers, pans and swamps. At other times they use coastal bush, riverine forest and wooded valleys.
summary: A common resident. The heavy bill is diagnostic. The breeding male is blackish-brown, with a white wing-spot and a white forehead, and a black bill. The female is dark brown above and whitish below, heavily streaked dark brown, with a horn-coloured bill. The immature is like the female with a yellower bill. Nesting birds chatter, and the male occasionally sings. The Kemp paper name Thickbilled Weaver and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Village Weaver is yellow, with a black mask and a spotted back. Thick-billed Weaver is dark, with a heavy bill.

calls.description: Nesting birds utter a monotonous chattering, and the male occasionally sings an almost musical song. Flocks give high-pitched calls in flight. Grade A song from Diani Beach, Kenya, with other species in the background. The filename is XC523322-ThickbilledWeaver_Diani_200126_0550_edited.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The non-breeding male, apart from the white forehead being a breeding mark, was not given a separate plumage. No female photograph and no flight photograph were found. The grade A song is from Kenya. Population figures and the Kemp name Thickbilled Weaver were left unchanged.
